material.goal: Determine whether DG-RWO-LANG-CONTRACT-001 and RWO-JCS-SAFEINT-V1 are precise enough for independent Python, Rust, and Go conformance, and produce verified KEEP/FIX requests before owner acceptance.
material.context: The existing contract proposes RFC 8785 canonical JSON, safe interoperable integers, NFC validation, SHA-256 identity, closed schemas, version rules, and immutable golden vectors. The review must challenge whether those rules are unambiguous at the byte, semantic, lifecycle, and owner boundaries without turning protobuf, gRPC, journals, retries, ARE, or runtime adoption into kernel identity. All target artifacts are read-only; outputs are private review evidence with authority_effect none and promotion_effect none.

predicted_disagreements.statement: Agent 0 runs a formal cross-language byte and schema proof while agent 1 runs an adversarial domain and lifecycle attack on the methodology axis; agent 1 exposes formally deterministic rules that still mis-own semantics or migration, while agent 0 exposes boundary objections that lack a discriminating byte-level counterexample.

agents.angle: formally prove or refute cross-language byte identity across canonicalization and schema edge cases
agents.initial_prompt: Role ID: formal-interop-reviewer. Dispatch: 2026-08-07-rwo-canonical-contract-dialectic-review. Attack the complete current corpus: projects/cyberalchemy-orchestrator/docs/features/recursive-work-orchestrator/development/decision-gates/20260807T144352Z-rwo-language-contract/{DG-RWO-LANG-CONTRACT-001.md,option-admissibility-request.json,option-admissibility-receipt.json}; projects/cyberalchemy-orchestrator/docs/features/recursive-work-orchestrator/development/refinement-runs/20260807T071542Z-rwo-language-selection/{RESULT.md,stages/06-invoke-design/DESIGN.md,stages/09-invoke-plan/PLAN.md}; projects/cyberalchemy-orchestrator/docs/features/recursive-work-orchestrator/development/refinement-runs/20260806T173343Z-rwo-composition-form-metamodel/refresh-runs/20260807T144352Z-rwo-language-oracle-waymaker/WAY-MAKER.md; and ops/development/2026-08-07-rwo-canonical-contract-dialectic-review/strategy-inventory-packet.json. Verify standards claims only against official RFC 8785, RFC 7493/I-JSON, Unicode normalization specifications, and official Protocol Buffers deterministic-serialization documentation; no broader web sources. Focus on JCS number behavior, negative zero, safe-integer boundaries, decimal-string grammar, Unicode/NFC and surrogate handling, object-key ordering, duplicate detection before map collapse, semantic collection ordering, version compatibility, digest domain separation, fixture-manifest recursion, independent expected-byte derivation, and Python/Rust/Go reproducibility. Do not edit files, decide the owner gate, implement code, or expand into transport/runtime design. Return: (1) 3-5 key findings with exact file:line or official-section evidence; (2) gaps/inconsistencies; (3) local tensions; (4) questions for synthesis; (5) per-artifact KEEP/FIX and one-line proposed fixes; (6) at least one discriminating positive or negative vector for every MAJOR finding; and (7) a lifecycle receipt containing agent_id, role_id, spawn_status, join_status, close_status, dispatch_id, reviewed identities, validation, blockers, residue, reroute, and handoff note. Findings without current evidence are speculation.

agents.angle: adversarially attack semantic sufficiency lifecycle evolution and transport ownership leakage
agents.initial_prompt: Role ID: domain-lifecycle-reviewer. Dispatch: 2026-08-07-rwo-canonical-contract-dialectic-review. Attack the same complete corpus listed for the formal lane, plus only the selected RWO current-state Inventory entry and its cited accepted findings as non-authority discovery context. Test whether the proposed profile actually defines semantic identity rather than merely stable JSON; whether type/domain separation prevents cross-type digest aliasing; whether unknown-field and minor-version rules are coherent; whether semantic ordering is fully schema-owned; whether canonical values, accepted-event identity, raw transport bytes, graph identity, cursor identity, and fixture identity are kept distinct; whether fixture generation can self-bless; and whether future protobuf/gRPC adapters, journals, retries, ARE, and runtime adoption remain consumers rather than owners. Use official standards only when challenging a standards claim. Do not edit files, choose the owner gate, implement code, design the service, or broaden into ontology promotion. Return the same mandatory Robot-Talks format: 3-5 evidenced key findings, gaps/inconsistencies, local tensions, synthesis questions, per-artifact KEEP/FIX with one-line fixes, discriminating scenarios for every MAJOR finding, and the complete lifecycle receipt fields. A policy preference without a concrete downstream ambiguity or counterexample is not a finding.
